implementation_notes: C# lambdas capture effectively-final locals, enforced by the compiler: a captured local must be declared with readonly or never reassigned, so late-binding surprises are compile errors rather than bugs. Since C# 9 a static lambda ('static (int x) => ...') is allowed and captures nothing - useful when the lambda is cached, because it keeps the closure alive and makes that lifetime explicit. Async lambdas ('async x => ...') are closures that capture the enclosing SynchronizationContext, which is how the continuation returns to the UI thread.
idiom_name: lambda expression capturing effectively-final locals; 'static lambda' for non-capturing
pitfalls: Capturing 'this' in an event handler subscribed to your own object is a classic retain cycle in long-lived (non-GC-scoped) hosts.
An async lambda captures the SynchronizationContext, so keeping one alive pins the whole UI context - pass explicit scheduling instead when the work outlives the window.
Closures cannot be tree-shaken or serialised; a lambda stored in configuration cannot be written to a settings file.
